A traversable functor is lawful if its `traverse` satisfies a
number of additional properties.  It must send `pure : α → Id α` to `pure`,
send the composition of applicative functors to the composition of the
`traverse` of each, send each function `f` to `fun x ↦ f <$> x`, and
satisfy a naturality condition with respect to applicative
transformations.

value.text:
| LawfulTraversable.mk.{u} {t : Type u → Type u} [Traversable t] [toLawfulFunctor : LawfulFunctor t]
  (id_traverse : ∀ {α : Type u} (x : t α), traverse pure x = pure x)
  (comp_traverse :
    ∀ {F G : Type u → Type u} [inst : Applicative F] [inst_1 : Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F]
      [LawfulApplicative G] {α β γ : Type u} (f : β → F γ) (g : α → G β) (x : t α),
      traverse (Functor.Comp.mk ∘ Functor.map f ∘ g) x =
        Functor.Comp.mk (traverse f <$> traverse g x))
  (traverse_eq_map_id :
    ∀ {α β : Type u} (f : α → β) (x : t α), traverse (pure ∘ f) x = pure (f <$> x))
  (naturality :
    ∀ {F G : Type u → Type u} [inst : Applicative F] [inst_1 : Applicative G] [LawfulApplicative F]
      [LawfulApplicative G] (η : ApplicativeTransformation F G) {α β : Type u} (f : α → F β)
      (x : t α), (fun {α} => η.app α) (traverse f x) = traverse ((fun {α} => η.app α) ∘ f) x) :
  LawfulTraversable t

doc:
Define `C v` by induction on `v : Vector α n`.

This function has two arguments: `nil` handles the base case on `C nil`,
and `cons` defines the inductive step using `∀ x : α, C w → C (x ::ᵥ w)`.

It is used as the default induction principle for the `induction` tactic.

value.text:
fun {α} {C} {n} v nil cons =>
  Nat.recAux (motive := fun {n} => (v : List.Vector α n) → C v)
    (fun v =>
      Subtype.casesOn v fun val property =>
        List.casesOn (motive := fun x => (property : x.length = 0) → C ⟨x, property⟩) val
          (fun property =>
            Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a x => 0 = a → property ≍ x → C ⟨[], property⟩) property
              (fun h h_1 => ⋯ ▸ nil) List.Vector.inductionOn._proof_3 ⋯)
          (fun head tail property =>
            Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a x => 0 = a → property ≍ x → C ⟨head :: tail, property⟩)
              property (fun h => False.elim ⋯) List.Vector.inductionOn._proof_3 ⋯)
          property)
    (fun n ih v =>
      Subtype.casesOn v fun val v_property =>
        List.casesOn (motive := fun x => (v_property : x.length = n + 1) → C ⟨x, v_property⟩) val
          (fun v_property =>
            Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a t => n + 1 = a → v_property ≍ t → C ⟨[], v_property⟩)
              v_property (fun h => False.elim ⋯) ⋯ ⋯)
          (fun a v v_property => cons (ih ⟨v, ⋯⟩)) v_property)
    n v

    {n : ℕ} →

  Nat.recAux (motive := fun {n} => (v : List.Vector α n) → (w : List.Vector β n) → C v w)
    (fun v w =>
      Subtype.casesOn v fun val property =>
        List.casesOn (motive := fun x => (property : x.length = 0) → C ⟨x, property⟩ w) val
          (fun property =>
            Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a x => 0 = a → property ≍ x → C ⟨[], property⟩ w) property
              (fun h h_1 =>
                ⋯ ▸
                  Subtype.casesOn w fun val property =>
                    List.casesOn (motive := fun x =>
                      (property : x.length = 0) → C ⟨[], ⋯⟩ ⟨x, property⟩) val
                      (fun property =>
                        Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a x =>
                          0 = a → property ≍ x → C ⟨[], ⋯⟩ ⟨[], property⟩) property
                          (fun h h_2 => ⋯ ▸ nil) List.Vector.inductionOn._proof_3 ⋯)
                      (fun head tail property =>
                        Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a x =>
                          0 = a → property ≍ x → C ⟨[], ⋯⟩ ⟨head :: tail, property⟩) property
                          (fun h => False.elim ⋯) List.Vector.inductionOn._proof_3 ⋯)
                      property)
              List.Vector.inductionOn._proof_3 ⋯)
          (fun head tail property =>
            Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a x => 0 = a → property ≍ x → C ⟨head :: tail, property⟩ w)
              property (fun h => False.elim ⋯) List.Vector.inductionOn._proof_3 ⋯)
          property)
    (fun n ih v w =>
      Subtype.casesOn v fun val v_property =>
        List.casesOn (motive := fun x => (v_property : x.length = n + 1) → C ⟨x, v_property⟩ w) val
          (fun v_property =>
            Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a t => n + 1 = a → v_property ≍ t → C ⟨[], v_property⟩ w)
              v_property (fun h => False.elim ⋯) ⋯ ⋯)
          (fun a v v_property =>
            Subtype.casesOn w fun val w_property =>
              List.casesOn (motive := fun x =>
                (w_property : x.length = n + 1) → C ⟨a :: v, v_property⟩ ⟨x, w_property⟩) val
                (fun w_property =>
                  Eq.casesOn (motive := fun a_1 t =>
                    n + 1 = a_1 → w_property ≍ t → C ⟨a :: v, v_property⟩ ⟨[], w_property⟩)
                    w_property (fun h => False.elim ⋯) ⋯ ⋯)
                (fun b w w_property => cons (ih ⟨v, ⋯⟩ ⟨w, ⋯⟩)) w_property)
          v_property)
    n v w

  [(i : ι) → Fintype (α i)] [CommMonoid M] (f : (i : ι) → α i → M) :
  ∏ x, f x.fst x.snd = ∏ x, ∏ y, f x y

theorem Fintype.prod_option.{u_1, u_4} {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_4} [Fintype α] [CommMonoid M]
  (f : Option α → M) : ∏ i, f i = f none * ∏ i, f (some i)
theorem Fintype.card_eq_sum_ones.{u_4} {α : Type u_4} [Fintype α] : Fintype.card α = ∑ _a, 1

theorem Fintype.sum_sumElim.{u_4, u_5, u_6} {α₁ : Type u_4} {α₂ : Type u_5} {M : Type u_6} [Fintype α₁]
  [Fintype α₂] [AddCommMonoid M] (f : α₁ → M) (g : α₂ → M) :
  ∑ x, Sum.elim f g x = ∑ a₁, f a₁ + ∑ a₂, g a₂
